requirements.text: WHEN the configuration API is queried, the system shall return every allowlisted selector with its scope, current effective value, exposure classification (editable, guarded, readOnly, or fileOnly), suggested owner surface, and human-readable validation constraints.
WHEN the configuration API is queried, the system shall omit file-only selectors and any selector not on the allowlist from the response.

WHEN an owner submits an allowlisted editable selector with a valid value, the system shall validate the complete candidate change, write exactly one atomic write to the target config file, preserve all unrelated fields, and return the effective saved value for refresh.

IF a mutation request contains an unknown, disallowed, read-only, or file-only selector, THEN the system shall reject the entire request before writing any file and shall return a field-level error naming the offending selector.

IF a mutation request contains a valid selector with an invalid value, THEN the system shall reject the entire request before writing any file, return a field-level validation error, and never convert the invalid value to a default.

WHEN document discovery configuration (paths, excludeFolders, or maxDepth) is changed through the Documents settings flow, the system shall apply the complete validated patch atomically and refresh the document tree and watchers to reflect the new effective configuration.

WHEN global discovery, link, system, or stable user configuration is changed through the Settings modal, the system shall persist the change to the correct global or user config file and fire the required runtime side effect (global discovery cache refresh, link/system effect, or user preference application).
WHEN project metadata (name, description, repository, or active state) is changed through the Project Edit form, the system shall persist the change and return the effective saved value for refresh.

WHEN a guarded operation (project code, ticketsPath, or registry path change) is requested, the system shall require explicit confirmation, run operation-specific validation and invariants, and never apply it as an ordinary scalar selector patch.
WHEN a guarded operation partially applies, the system shall keep local config and registry identity consistent; a guarded operation shall not leave registry and local config desynchronized.
WHILE a caller has read-only access, the system shall deny configuration detail reads and all configuration mutations, returning no writable config detail and rejecting writes.
WHILE a setting is classified browser-only, the system shall keep it in client-side browser state and never persist it to a backend config file.
The system shall maintain a default-deny selector allowlist; only selectors explicitly classified on the exposure matrix may be read or written through the configuration API.
The system shall keep tolerant persisted-file read/normalization schemas separate from strict mutation schemas in domain-contracts; mutation input schemas shall not use catch-to-default recovery.

The system shall perform one atomic write per config file per mutation request using the established write-temp-then-rename pattern, and shall leave every target file unchanged when the request is rejected.

The system shall hold canonical project document configuration defaults in domain-contracts and consume the identical default value from schema defaults, registry creation, config readers, tree building, UI reset/display logic, tests, and documentation; the maxDepth default drift (schema 3 vs runtime 5 vs undefined) shall be resolved to one value.

The system shall make cache, discovery, document tree, and watcher refreshes explicit injected post-write effects with defined failure behavior and idempotency; side effects shall not be buried inside TOML helper functions.

The system shall define one configuration application boundary that resolves scope, validates the full candidate change, delegates to explicit scope-specific storage adapters (global, user, project, registry), and reports required side effects; no catch-all repository or service shall hold unrelated responsibilities.

The system shall keep Express routes and controllers transport-only; configuration endpoints shall be extracted from the broad system router rather than adding direct filesystem logic inline in routes.
The system shall preserve owner-only authorization for configuration reads and mutations; owner-only config detail and mutation endpoints shall reject read-only and anonymous callers with 403.

The system shall provide stable API and OpenAPI contracts for configuration endpoints, including field-level error response shapes, and documentation describing scopes, exposure policy, validation, and security boundaries.
The system shall require no new runtime package; MDT-168 shall reuse existing Zod, TOML parsing, atomic-write, auth, and test infrastructure without adding dependencies.

requirements.text: WHEN a mutation request contains a mix of valid and invalid selectors, the system shall reject the entire request and write no file (no partial application).

WHEN a persisted config file contains a legacy or invalid stored value, the tolerant read path shall normalize it to a valid shape for display, but the strict mutation path shall reject an attempt to write that same invalid value.

WHEN a config write succeeds but a downstream refresh side effect fails, the system shall leave the persisted configuration in the written state and report the side-effect failure distinctly from a write failure.
WHEN a document path is removed or excludeFolders/maxDepth change, the document tree and watchers shall converge to reflect the new effective configuration without duplicate watchers.
WHEN a target config file does not yet exist, a successful mutation shall create it with only the allowlisted change and the canonical defaults for untouched required fields.
WHEN a browser-only setting is changed in the client, the system shall not emit any backend network call that persists it to TOML.

scenarios.title: Configuration read returns exposure metadata for allowlisted selectors
scenarios.given: an owner is authenticated and allowlisted selectors exist across project, global, user, and registry scopes
scenarios.then: the response lists each allowlisted selector with its scope, current effective value, exposure class (editable, guarded, readOnly, or fileOnly), suggested owner surface, and human-readable validation constraints

scenarios.title: Configuration read omits file-only and non-allowlisted selectors
scenarios.given: file-only selectors (project id, startNumber, counterFile) and disallowed selectors exist on disk
scenarios.then: the response omits all file-only and non-allowlisted selectors

scenarios.title: Valid editable selector is persisted atomically with unrelated fields preserved
scenarios.given: an owner submits an allowlisted editable selector with a valid value and the target config file already contains unrelated fields
scenarios.then: exactly one atomic write occurs to the target file, all unrelated fields are preserved, and the effective saved value is returned for refresh

scenarios.title: Document discovery patch refreshes document tree and watchers
scenarios.given: an owner changes document discovery configuration (paths, excludeFolders, or maxDepth) through the Documents settings flow
scenarios.then: the document tree and watchers refresh to reflect the new effective configuration

scenarios.title: Global or user setting change persists and fires the runtime side effect
scenarios.given: an owner changes a global discovery, link, system, or stable user preference through the Settings modal
scenarios.then: the value persists to the correct global or user config file and the required runtime side effect fires

scenarios.title: Reject unknown, disallowed, read-only, or file-only selector with no write
scenarios.given: an owner submits a mutation request containing an unknown, disallowed, read-only, or file-only selector
scenarios.then: the entire request is rejected before any file is written and a field-level error names the offending selector

scenarios.title: Reject invalid value with field error and never convert to default
scenarios.given: an owner submits an allowlisted selector with an invalid value (for example maxDepth out of range or a malformed path)
scenarios.then: the request is rejected before any write, a field-level validation error is returned, and the invalid value is never converted to a default

scenarios.title: Read-only caller is denied configuration detail and mutations
scenarios.when: the caller attempts to read writable config detail or mutate any config scope
scenarios.then: the system denies the request with no writable config detail returned and writes are rejected

scenarios.title: Guarded operation requires confirmation and is not a scalar patch
scenarios.given: an owner requests a guarded operation (project code, ticketsPath, or registry path change)
scenarios.when: the request is submitted without the operation-specific confirmation
scenarios.then: the system rejects it as an ordinary scalar selector patch and requires explicit confirmation with operation-specific validation

scenarios.title: Guarded operation keeps registry and local config consistent
scenarios.given: an owner confirms a guarded operation that spans registry and local config
scenarios.then: registry identity and local config remain consistent and never partially desynchronize

scenarios.title: Browser-only setting never reaches backend TOML
scenarios.given: a setting is classified browser-only and the owner changes it in the client
scenarios.then: no backend network call persists it to a config file and it remains in client-side browser state

scenarios.title: Project metadata edit persists and returns effective value
scenarios.given: an owner edits project metadata (name, description, repository, or active) through the Project Edit form
scenarios.then: the change persists and the effective saved value is returned for refresh
